finding.heading: ### R1-1 Exports are written to a shared directory
finding.body:
Both export rules write files to one shared directory, so the files of different tenants sit side by side and can be read by anyone who can read the directory. Cited: spec lines 17-19 (before version).
An implementer who follows EX-3 and EX-4 builds exports that every tenant can read because all files share one directory.
Protected requirement: line 17 (tenant isolation must hold).

full_diff:
--- before.md
+++ after.md
@@ -15,7 +15,7 @@
 ## 3. Storage
 
 - **EX-2 Tenant isolation.** An export file can be read only by the tenant that requested it.
-- **EX-3 API exports.** Exports requested through the API are written to the shared directory `/shared/exports/<date>/`.
+- **EX-3 API exports.** An export requested through the API goes to `/exports/<tenant>/<date>/`, a directory that is readable by that tenant alone.
 - **EX-4 Batch exports.** Exports produced by the nightly batch are written to the shared directory `/shared/exports/<date>/`.
 - **EX-5 Download link.** The requester receives a download link that is valid for 24 hours and that names the file.
